title: Envelope v1 — shared definitions
description: Definitions shared by envelope-inbound.v1.json and envelope-outbound.v1.json. Nothing validates against this file directly. The envelope is the outside of every message: everything the relay needs to route it without opening the payload.

uuidV4.description: A lowercase UUID version 4. Enforced by pattern rather than `format` so every language checks it identically.

nilUuid.description: The nil UUID. Used as runId on messages that belong to no run.

runId.description: The run this message belongs to, or the nil UUID when it belongs to none.

utcTimestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time in UTC, always ending in `Z`, with optional fractional seconds. Enforced by pattern rather than `format` so every language checks it identically.

common.description: Fields every envelope carries, in both directions.

id.description: Identifies this message. A message re-sent after a reconnect keeps its id, so a receiver drops an id it has already handled.

type.description: What the payload is. Selects the payload schema.

envelopeVersion.description: Version of this envelope's shape — not of the payload. Only 1 exists.

session.description: The session this message belongs to. Absent — the key missing, never an empty string — until a session exists.

to.description: Where the message goes. The relay routes on this alone.

traceId.description: Correlates one user action across every hop and every log line.

sentAt.description: The sender's clock when it sent the message. Informational only: a wrong clock never gets a message rejected. relay.receivedAt is the authoritative time.

payload.description: The content. Its shape is defined by the schema `type` names; the envelope only requires an object here. The relay opens it only when `to` is `relay`.

relayBlock.description: Written by the relay on every message it delivers. Never supplied by a sender.

from.description: Who sent the message, taken from the authenticated connection it arrived on — never from the message.

receivedAt.description: The relay's clock when the message arrived, or when the relay created it. The authoritative time for ordering, timeouts and recordings.

sequence.description: Position in this session's stream to this receiver, starting at 1. A reconnecting device sends the last one it saw in hello.lastSeenSequence and the relay resends everything after it.
